other_height_rules: Where no BFE has been established in an SFHA: at least 2 ft above highest adjacent grade. AO zones: FIRM depth number plus 2 ft freeboard above highest adjacent grade (or at least 2 ft above HAG if no depth number).
quote: “Regulatory Flood Protection Elevation” means the “Base Flood Elevation” plus the “Freeboard”. In “Special Flood Hazard Areas” where Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus two (2) feet freeboard. In “Special Flood Hazard Areas” where no BFE has been established, this elevation shall be at least two (2) feet above the highest adjacent grade.
date_quote: This ordinance shall become effective December 21, 2018. ... I hereby certify that this is a true and correct copy of the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance as adopted by the Board of Commissioners of Pasquotank County, North Carolina, on the 5th day of November, 2018.
notes: Current 2 ft confirmed in the official county FDPO (adopted 2018-11-05, effective 2018-12-21 with new FIRMs) and in the Albemarle Regional HMP (March 2025): 'Camden County, Chowan County, Edenton, Gates County, Gatesville, and Pasquotank County have a two-foot freeboard requirement' (https://perquimanscountync.gov/component/phocadownload/category/5-emergency-management?download=1909%3Aalbemarle-regional-hazard-mitigation-plan). The 2018 ordinance re-enacts the FDPO 'enacted January 3, 1976, as amended', so the 2018 date is the earliest CONFIRMED date of the 2 ft, not proven first adoption. Evidence of 0 ft earlier: the Pasquotank County/Elizabeth City CAMA Land Use Plan (adopted 2012-01-09, drafted ~2004-05; https://www.pasquotankcountync.org/s/Feb-82012-revised-LUP-ecac.pdf) lists a July 2005 Hazard Mitigation Plan action to 'Amend the Pasquotank County Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance ... to increase the minimum lowest floor elevation of structures located within flood hazard areas to 1 feet above the base flood elevation', implying no county freeboard c.2005 (ordinance then cited as 'August 1994'). Whether 1 ft (or 2 ft) was adopted between 2005 and 2018 was not found; Wayback Machine was unreachable from this environment. A citizenportal.ai item (2026-04-06, paywalled) says the board is considering raising freeboard from 2 to 3-4 ft or regulating the 0.2% floodplain in the new UDO; not adopted as of that source.

history.quote: REGULATORY FLOOD PROTECTION ELEVATION. The elevation, in relation to mean sea level, to which the reference level of all structures and other development located within special flood hazard areas must be protected. Residential construction within areas where Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus one foot of freeboard. Commercial construction required to meet or exceed BFE. In areas where no BFE has been established, residential construction elevation shall be at least four feet above the highest adjacent grade. (Note: four feet above highest adjacent grade includes freeboard.)

other_height_rules: 2015 code: where no BFE established, residential at least 4 ft above highest adjacent grade (includes freeboard); commercial 2 ft above HAG with no freeboard; commercial in BFE areas only to BFE (0 ft). Current (post-2019 UDO) no-BFE rule not verified.
quote: Additionally, several participating jurisdictions have some local standards that exceed state requirements. For example, Camden County, Chowan County, Edenton, Gates County, Gatesville, and Pasquotank County have a two-foot freeboard requirement; Elizabeth City requires a three-foot freeboard.

A 2015-04-20 printout of the old Chapter 151 (American Legal) shows BFE + 1 ft for RESIDENTIAL construction and BFE + 0 for commercial. The flood article was re-enacted by Ord. 2004-09-01 (passed 2004-10-04, with the 2004-10-05 FIRMs) and the definitions were amended repeatedly 2003-2012, so the 1 ft likely dates from 2004 or later but its start year was not confirmed. The change from 1 ft to 2 ft happened between April 2015 and March 2025 (plausibly with the Dec 2018 FIRMs or the Feb 2019 UDO) but no dated source was found; Ord. 2015-06-03 (adopted 2015-08-03, flood amendments) did not change the freeboard and Ord. 2019-08-02 contains no freeboard text. Wayback Machine unreachable from this environment.

other_height_rules: Where no BFE has been established in an SFHA: at least 3 ft above highest adjacent grade (both Ord. No. 99 of 2018 and draft/adopted Ord. No. 112 of 2026).
quote: “Regulatory Flood Protection Elevation” means the “Base Flood Elevation” plus the “Freeboard”. In “Special Flood Hazard Areas” where Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus zero (0) feet freeboard). In “Special Flood Hazard Areas” where no BFE has been established, this elevation shall be at least three (3) feet above the highest adjacent grade.
date_quote: On motion made by Edward R. Muzzulin, seconded by Fondella A. Leigh, the Board unanimously adopted Ordinance No. 99 – Flood Plan Prevention Ordinance (see Attachment A).
notes: No local freeboard (0 ft = NFIP minimum) in every version found. Ord. No. 99 (adopted 2018-11-05; scanned PDF at https://www.perquimanscountync.gov/county-information/ordinances?download=24:flood-plain-prevention-ordinance, page footer 'November 5, 2018', read by rendering page 9 to an image) has the identical 'BFE plus zero (0) feet freeboard' definition. Draft Ord. No. 112 'Replaces Ordinance No. 99', cover says 'Adopted by the Perquimans County Board of Commissioners on September 8, 2026' and keeps 0 ft (BOC page lists it as DRAFT for the 2026-09-08 hearing and 2026-10-05 meeting; adoption status not confirmed). The ordinance re-enacts the FDPO 'enacted April 9, 1985, as amended'; versions between 1985 and 2018 were not seen, so current_since_year and history_complete are left null/false. Albemarle Regional HMP (March 2025) does not list Perquimans among jurisdictions with freeboard. State building code (NC Residential Code) freeboard applies separately and is not recorded here.

other_height_rules: Ocracoke village (Ocracoke Development Ordinance): per Ocracoke Observer 2020-02-24, the minimum living-floor level was 'seven feet, ... one foot above mean high tide of six feet'; the planning board proposed 8 ft, then recommended (2020-03) 'a uniform height of nine feet above mean high tide'. Adoption of that ODO change not confirmed. 2012 Ocracoke permit package: 'All mechanical, electrical and duct work will have to be 1 foot above the base flood elevation.'
quote: Washington County, Creswell, Plymouth, Roper, and Columbia have a two-foot freeboard requirement; Hyde County and Tyrrell County require a one-foot freeboard. [same plan, action H1:] Consider revising the county's Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance to increase the current established two foot freeboard requirement regarding base flood elevation for new structures developed within the Flood Hazard Area.
date_quote: Hyde County can and intends to adopt a Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance that requires new constructions and building elevations be higher than the new flood maps recommend. ... The Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance will add an additional freeboard requirement. ... On June 1, 2020 at 6:00pm in conjunction with the regular Hyde County Board of Commissioners meeting, a final public hearing will be held and the board will vote to adopt the flood maps and the new flood ordinance. (Island Free Press, 2020-05-14)
notes: Current value UNRESOLVED: the Northeastern NC Regional HMP (approved April 2021) contradicts itself - capability assessment says Hyde requires 1 ft, its action H1 says 'current established two foot freeboard'. The county ordinance itself could not be read: hydecountync.gov and cms2.revize.com/revize/hydecounty pages return HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch, WNCT article 403, and the session's web-search budget ran out. History clues: the 2017 Regional HMP (FEMA-approved 2017-07-07, https://cms2.revize.com/revize/hydecounty/departments/docs/Adopted%20RHMP_7%207%202017.pdf) action H1 was 'Consider revising the county's Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance to establish a one foot freeboard requirement regarding base flood elevation for new structures', implying no FDPO freeboard c.2016-17; May 2020 news says the new FDPO (vote planned 2020-06-01 with new FIRMs effective June 2020) 'will add an additional freeboard requirement'. So FDPO freeboard most likely began with the June 2020 ordinance (1 or 2 ft), but adoption date and value were not confirmed from the ordinance. Conflicting older clue: the 2012 Ocracoke building permit package (https://cms2.revize.com/revize/hydecounty/departments/docs/Ocracoke_building_permit_package___4_20_12.pdf) says 'Hyde County has incorporated 1 foot of freeboard', in the context of mechanical/electrical/duct work; it may refer to utilities only or to a non-FDPO rule. Needs a direct read of the 2020 Hyde FDPO.

quote: Additionally, several of the participating jurisdictions have some local standards that exceed state requirements. For example, Washington County, Creswell, Plymouth, Roper, and Columbia have a two-foot freeboard requirement; Hyde County and Tyrrell County require a one-foot freeboard.
notes: Only source found is the Northeastern NC Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan (Bertie, Hyde, Martin, Tyrrell, Washington; 'Approved April 2021'), capability assessment section 5.3.6. The same paragraph's Hyde figure conflicts with Hyde's own action item (1 ft vs 2 ft), so treat this value as unverified. The county ordinance could not be reached: tyrrellcounty.org returned 503 / no connection, other candidate domains were refused by the egress proxy, no Municode listing, and the session's web-search budget was exhausted. The 2017 Regional HMP (https://cms2.revize.com/revize/hydecounty/departments/docs/Adopted%20RHMP_7%207%202017.pdf) contains no Tyrrell freeboard statement. Adoption year of the 1 ft and the earlier history are unknown.
